question: Let $A$ and $B$ be independent events with $P(A)=\frac{2}{5}$ and $P(B)=\frac{3}{7}$. Establish that $A$ and $B'$ are also independent and hence determine $P(A\cup B')$.
explanation:
Required Condition
Since $A$ and $B$ are independent,
$$P(A\cap B)=P(A)P(B)=\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{3}{7}=\frac{6}{35}.$$
Also,
$$P(B')=1-P(B)=1-\frac{3}{7}=\frac{4}{7}.$$

The event $A$ can be written as the disjoint union of $A\cap B$ and $A\cap B'$. Hence,
$$P(A\cap B')=P(A)-P(A\cap B)=\frac{2}{5}-\frac{6}{35}=\frac{14-6}{35}=\frac{8}{35}.$$
On the other hand,
$$P(A)P(B')=\frac{2}{5}\times\frac{4}{7}=\frac{8}{35}.$$
Thus,
$$P(A\cap B')=P(A)P(B'),$$
which establishes that $A$ and $B'$ are independent.

Evaluation
Using the addition rule,
$$P(A\cup B')=P(A)+P(B')-P(A\cap B').$$
Therefore,
$$P(A\cup B')=\frac{2}{5}+\frac{4}{7}-\frac{8}{35}=\frac{14+20-8}{35}=\frac{26}{35}.$$

Final Result
Hence, $A$ and $B'$ are independent and $P(A\cup B')=\frac{26}{35}$.
